title: When the Hymn Sings
premise: Marguerite Thornbury's late-night call-in show becomes a séance when the voices on the line belong to residents of Hollow Creek who died the previous week, all reciting the same hymn. As she documents the calls, she realizes the town's founding families signed a covenant generations ago: every twenty-five years, the last surviving resident must 'sign the papers,' surrendering the town's children to whatever waits beneath the church. Her childhood imaginary friend, Elias, appears on her porch unchanged, warning that she was always meant to be the final signature. Marguerite must choose between the loyalty that kept her invisible and safe, and the truth that could free the town, ultimately burning the covenant and her recordings, erasing her show, her archive, and nearly herself, so the last resident dies unsigned and the children walk free.
about_author: Lena Blackwood spent a decade as a small-market radio producer before turning to horror, and she still can't sleep without static in the background. She writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York where, she insists, the phone lines are perfectly ordinary.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. During her 2 a.m. call-in show, a woman phones in to request a hymn; Marguerite recognizes the voice as Dora Pell, buried six days ago. Shaken, she begins recording every call, telling herself documentation is a kind of prayer. The beat is dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Cross-referencing call logs with obituaries, she confirms seven dead callers, all founding-family descendants, all humming the same verse. At the cemetery she finds fresh footprints around Dora's grave, leading nowhere. Emotional beat: the comfort of pattern curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Elias, Unchanged
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Her childhood imaginary friend is sitting on the porch, exactly as she left him at nine years old, down to the missing button. He says he's been waiting and that she was never invisible, only deferred. Beat: tenderness laced with violation.

chapters.title: What the Church Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite, with flashbacks to age nine. In the sealed church basement she finds the covenant: signatures every twenty-five years, the final line reserved for a 'Thornbury.' The dead callers were signatories released early. Beat: the past stops being childhood and becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Loyal Listeners
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The living townspeople turn on her gently, lovingly, urging her to stop the show, bring pies, remind her how her family was spared in the last count because they kept quiet. Beat: loyalty revealed as a leash, and the horror of being loved conditionally.

chapters.title: The Verse Reversed
chapters.summary: POV Elias. The imaginary friend narrates what he is: a placeholder, a name held in trust until Marguerite came of signing age. He loves her in the only way he was built to. Beat: sympathy for the instrument, and Marguerite's identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She uses the show to broadcast the truth, urging families to leave before the count completes. Some go; some report her to the council. Her station is padlocked, her tapes seized. Beat: the price of truth made literal, her voice taken.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The final surviving signatory, old Amos Wren, is wheeled to the church to sign. Marguerite breaks in, and Elias stands between her and the papers, offering to take the signature himself if she'll just stay invisible, just this once. Beat: the temptation of safety.

chapters.title: Burn the Hymn
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She refuses, feeds the covenant and every recording of the dead callers into the church furnace while the hymn screams out of the speakers. Elias unravels into static in her arms. Amos dies unsigned. Beat: grief and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The town empties; the station goes dark; no one remembers the show but her. On an empty highway she pulls over at a porch where a child is talking to someone unseen, and Marguerite, changed, sits down to listen. Beat: survival with a scar, truth carried forward.
